Arthur Hayes: High-FDV Shitcoins Can't Even Pump on Binance Anymore

Flop Labs CEO Arthur Hayes said in an October 16 interview with LukeMartin that the entire crypto industry has abused tokenomics. From ICOs to VC private sales and presales, some projects raise funds supposedly to build products, only to dump tokens after launching protocols and unlocking allocations. Retail investors buying at TGE suffer heavy losses, sometimes watching token prices plunge 95%. Hayes argued that retail investors increasingly see through the high-FDV, low-float model, saying such tokens "can't even pump on Binance anymore." He favors projects like Hyperliquid, which have genuine product-market fit, return revenue to token holders, and avoid massive sell pressure from presold token unlocks. — link

Arthur Hayes: Maelstrom Has Closed Its Directional Positions, Taking Profits on ETH, ENA and UNI

Arthur Hayes said Maelstrom has closed all positions in its directional trading book, taking profits on ETH, ENA, UNI and other altcoins. He believes the market may need to fall before rising, citing uncertainty surrounding macroeconomic and geopolitical conditions. He plans to remain on the sidelines and wait for an all-clear signal.

According to @EmberCN, Arthur Hayes reduced his holdings in various tokens totaling approximately $26.08 million, including 8,000 ETH (approx. $19 million), 14 million ENA (approx. $2.76 million), and 323,000 UNI (approx. $2.24 million). — link

Swell Pauses swETH and rswETH Deposits and Withdrawals Amid Abnormally High Contract Exchange Rates

According to Unchained, Ethereum staking protocol Swell has paused deposits and withdrawals for swETH and rswETH until it corrects the net asset values (NAV) and exchange rates of both tokens. Data shows that the swETH and rswETH contracts reported exchange rates of approximately 1.203 ETH and 1.138 ETH, respectively, about 6% and 5% higher than normal levels.

On-chain analyst Spreek suspected a compromise of the relevant token admin keys and identified a malicious upgrade contract that could potentially impact around 2,500 ETH, though the upgrade has not yet been executed. Swell stated that no ETH has been transferred out of the affected contracts and that the exact cause remains under investigation. — link

Tether's Bitcoin Mining Development Kit Gains Backing from 15 Mining Companies to Accelerate Automated Mining

Tether announced that its open-source Mining Development Kit (MDK) has secured joint support and integration commitments from 15 leading mining companies, ASIC manufacturers, and mining pools, including Bitmain, Bitdeer, Canaan, MicroBT, Foundry Digital, F2Pool, Luxor, and Block's Proto. By establishing a unified open interface, the kit breaks down barriers between disparate hardware and mining pools, aiming to accelerate AI- and software-driven cross-platform automated dispatch and autonomous operations for physical mining infrastructure. MDK released version 0.11 at the Plan ₿ Forum in Lugano, with a stable 1.0 release targeted by the end of 2026. — link

Keystone Confirms Customer Data Exposure Following Unauthorized Website Access

Keystone Hardware Wallet confirmed that a third party obtained customer shipping and order information following unauthorized access to its official website. The incident was detected on October 20, with the data exposure confirmed on October 23 after reviewing API activity with Shopify. Exposed information included names, contact details, shipping addresses, purchased items, and prices. Payment card and bank details, recovery phrases, private keys, and wallet passwords were not exposed. Keystone said it has blocked the access, fixed the vulnerability, and is notifying affected customers. It also warned of impersonation scams involving fake refunds, replacement devices, or order fixes.

Keystone said its latest investigation found that attackers obtained a WebAuth device-authentication key through the website breach, potentially allowing counterfeit hardware wallets to pass official authenticity checks. The company will destroy 18,835 unsold devices using the old key, pause unshipped orders and switch new production to a replacement key. The incident also affected 25,964 purchase records and 12,873 incomplete checkout records, while Keystone said seed phrases, private keys and transaction signing were not compromised. — link
